title: Decouple routing telemetry buffer and transition manager to reduce hotpath locking
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: The smart routing hotpath currently performs synchronous telemetry aggregation and transition/state updates under shared locks. This causes contention during traffic spikes (particularly for short-running requests at high QPS) and amplifies tail latency. We observed amplification in the p95/p99 during the 2026-01-18 regional surge incident.

Goal: Reduce lock contention and tail latency by separating the telemetry buffering path from the routing transition manager. Introduce a lock-free telemetry buffer (ring buffer + atomic write offsets) and convert transition/state propagation to an async, eventual-consistent signal flow with bounded staleness. Preserve correctness of fallback decisions and quota checks while improving throughput and tail.

Scope:
- Implement a lock-free telemetry buffer that sampling/aggregator threads can write to without taking the routing mutex.
- Replace synchronous transition calls on the request path with an in-process async signal that queues transition work to a prioritized worker pool.
- Add bounded backpressure and metrics to ensure transition queue does not grow unbounded.
- Maintain a compatibility shim so older regional policy adapters continue to read routing state until they are migrated.
- Provide migration toggle (feature flag) and rollout plan per region.

Success criteria (quantitative):
- p95 request latency on smart-router hotpath reduced by >= 10% in synthetic high-concurrency tests.
- p99 reduced by >= 5% (goal).
- No increase in incorrect fallback events (regression <= 0.1% of fallback decisions).
- Transition queue stays < 2000 items under expected peak load in staging.

Non-goals: Full redesign of policy evaluator or regional affinity heuristics; this ticket focuses on hotpath contention and telemetry decoupling only.
acceptance_criteria: Lock-free telemetry buffer implemented and exposed behind feature flag
Transition manager runs in an async worker pool and is plumbed with bounded queueing
End-to-end regression tests validate fallback correctness with async transitions
Benchmarks showing p95/p99 improvements and no fallback correctness regressions
Rollout plan and per-region toggles documented in the runbook
steps_taken: 2026-02-12: Investigated contention with flame graphs from the 2026-01-18 incident; identified telemetry aggregation and synchronous transition propagation as hotspots
2026-02-20: Spike implementation of ring buffer and async worker pool in sandbox branch (git: https://github.com/redwood-inference/smart-router/pull/2281)
2026-02-27: Benchmarked spike under synthetic load; observed ~14% p95 improvement but occasional transition lag—added backpressure metrics to plan
2026-03-03: Design review with Runtime and Observability teams; agreed on telemetry export contract and rollout toggles
decisions: Use a single-producer/multi-consumer ring buffer with atomic offsets to avoid per-write mutexes
Transition manager will be eventual-consistent with max staleness window of 500ms by default
Prioritized worker pool: emergency transitions (circuit open/close, capacity signals) get higher priority than telemetry flushes
Feature flag will be region-scoped and controlled via console rollout APIs
tests: Unit tests for ring buffer concurrent writers/readers (deterministic stress harness)
Integration test: compare fallback decisions vs baseline for 100k synthetic requests across region-sharded policies
Load test in staging running 10k QPS for 10 minutes with toggle on/off and measure p95/p99
Chaos test: simulate worker pool saturation and verify bounded backpressure behavior
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Merge behind feature flag and run non-traffic e2e tests in CI
Stage 1: Enable in preprod region (us-west-2) with 1% traffic for 24h, monitor telemetry and fallback mismatch rate
Stage 2: Ramp to 25% over 48h, then 100% in preprod if stable
Stage 3: Enable region-by-region for production with 0->10->50->100 ramps and guardrails (fallback-mismatch > 0.1% or transition-queue > 2000 triggers rollback)
Rollback: feature-flag toggle and emergency kill-switch via console; runbook steps documented
notes: Observability: add histogram for transition latency (enqueue->dequeue), gauge for queue length, and counter for dropped transitions due to backpressure
Compatibility: policy adapters must be migrated to read state snapshots from the new state-view cache; shim will present consistent snapshot API
Cost: worker pool will add nominal CPU; expected cost delta < 2% for routing tier under normal load
Related design: see policy-eval migration doc linked in dependencies
